body:
This is the fixed proposed by my agent, I'm nowhere near to have enough expertise to real review it with a critical view, but as far as I can tell it looks right and I hope it'll be useful. Feel free to close the PR if you think of a better fix, or take it over if it's close enough to be mergeable. Thanks! :pray: 

-----

Fixes #8120.

`nowait` now stays only where no barrier is needed:

- when the GIL is held, where the implicit barrier would deadlock and the explicit one after `PyEval_SaveThread()` replaces it
- on a standalone `prange`, since the end of the parallel region follows
- on a `prange` that ends a `parallel` block, for the same reason

Every other `prange` in a `parallel` block is back to a plain `omp for`, as in 3.2. I kept `nowait` in the last two cases because clang doesn't remove a redundant end barrier, and GCC doesn't always either.

This has a cost compared to 3.3 and almost none compared to 3.2. In scikit-learn, median of 6 runs in s, on one socket of a Xeon (86 threads) and on a Core Ultra 9 285 (24 threads), with libgomp:

| case | machine, wait policy | 3.2.4 | 3.3.1 | patched |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| KMeans lloyd | Xeon, passive | 0.667 | 0.520 | 0.667 |
| KMeans elkan | Xeon, passive | 1.028 | 0.815 | 1.023 |
| t-SNE | Xeon, passive | 2.275 | 1.975 | 2.239 |
| KMeans lloyd | Xeon, default | 0.526 | 0.459 | 0.514 |
| KMeans elkan | Xeon, default | 0.698 | 0.674 | 0.701 |
| t-SNE | Xeon, default | 1.182 | 1.059 | 1.063 |
| KMeans lloyd | Core Ultra 9, default | 0.184 | 0.173 | 0.184 |
| KMeans elkan | Core Ultra 9, default | 0.566 | 0.533 | 0.557 |
| t-SNE | Core Ultra 9, default | 0.899 | 0.777 | 0.871 |

So up to 28% slower than 3.3.1 with a passive runtime. These loops run code after the `prange` (a reduction under a lock, `free()` of thread-local buffers) that doesn't depend on the other threads, so they don't need the wait, but Cython can't know that.

ArgKmin, RadiusNeighbors and HGB predict stay within 2% of 3.3.1 on the Xeon with a passive runtime. HGB fits don't change: all the loops of `histogram.c` and `splitting.c` are standalone, and their function bodies are identical to 3.3.1.

These timings come from a slightly earlier version of the patch, which also kept the barrier on a `prange` that ends a `parallel` block. None of the KMeans and t-SNE loops above ends its block, so that doesn't change them.

The new tests in `tests/run/parallel.pyx` fail without the patch: `test_prange_end_barrier` returns 3 instead of 0 with GCC, and the generated clauses are checked for two loops in one block. Cython's parallel tests pass in C and C++ with GCC 15 on master (211d68e59). Nothing was run on Windows.

With clang, `tests/run/parallel_with_gil.pyx` still hangs on GIL builds. That's a separate bug, it's the same on master, and this patch doesn't touch it.

An explicit `prange(..., nowait=True)` could give the speed of 3.3 back to loops that know they don't need the wait. I haven't implemented it. Would you want that, here or as a follow-up?

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

comment_data.body:
I'm never hugely keen on these `test_assert_c_code_has` tests.  As I understand it Cython used to be tested by matching C code generation (in the distant past, long before I was involved with it) but that proved to be pretty fragile and so was dropped. We (reluctantly) re-added these asserts recently for the rare cases where there's no other way. But for some reason AI seems pretty keen to use them as much as possible.

It's also a fairly big file so pretty easy to accidentally get a false match.

I guess there isn't really another way of testing the special-casing for the last loop though. Maybe make the variable name a little more distinctive (e.g. `test_prange_barrier_between_loops_last_loop_target` just to reduce the chance of an accidental clash)

comment_data.body:
The other thing we could do is put a manual `#pragma omp barrier` here (but without the GIL handling stuff) in the case it's needed and leave the '#pragma omp for noawait` unchanged. That has the advantage that it keeps related logic in one place. But maybe the disadvantage that it's a less natural form for OpenMP so might be less optimized?

If it's quick to rerun the benchmarks I wouldn't mind trying that? I think I'd prefer it if it was the same speed (but would go with what you have if it's worse)

It probably isn't worth fixing actually in that it's code that shouldn't ever get run (and if it does run then it'll trip the test whether or not the count is strictly accurate). So it's maybe just that `with gil:` is giving a false impression of a meaningful lock

comment_data.body:
I tried it: `omp for nowait` everywhere, and an explicit `#pragma omp barrier` after the loop when code follows it (but not for a nested `prange`, where it would end up inside the outer loop).

With GCC it's the same speed. Both versions compile to the same 465 GOMP_barrier call sites in scikit-learn (399 with 3.3.1), and the timings match within noise. 

With clang it costs one more barrier. Clang keeps a barrier at the end of a loop with lastprivate even with nowait, so between two prange loops it runs 3 barriers in a row (its own, the explicit one, and the one at the start of the next loop), against 2 with this PR. I checked that in the object code of a two-loop example with clang 21.

But actually, with another PR/fix I'm working on, this approach could maybe have no cost / a near-zero cost.

I pushed it: every `prange` is now `omp for nowait`, with an explicit `#pragma omp barrier` after it when code follows in the `parallel` block. I removed the two `test_assert_c_code_has` lines, since every loop has the same pragma now.

On scikit-learn, it seems the cost of the extra clang barrier is small and only visible on a big server with `OMP_WAIT_POLICY=passive` which is a non-default and weird setting.

With GCC, both versions compile to the same code.

It should get even smaller with the other PR/fix I mentioned in https://github.com/cython/cython/issues/8129#issuecomment-6767596911.

commit.message:
Keep the end barrier of prange when code follows it in a parallel block

GH-6562 made every prange "omp for nowait" but only added an explicit barrier on the path that holds the GIL. In nogil code, the statements after a prange in a parallel block could run before the other threads finished. A prange that ends the block doesn't need a barrier, since the end of the parallel region follows.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Address review: clearer nowait choice, test names and placement

Choose nowait only in the branch where it can vary, and keep the literal
"omp for nowait" for a standalone prange. Give the loop targets checked
by test_assert_c_code_has longer names, to avoid false matches. Move
test_prange_end_barrier to sequential_parallel.pyx so that it also runs
without OpenMP, and make its counter a flag, since "with gil" isn't a
lock on free-threaded builds.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commit.message:
Use "omp for nowait" and an explicit barrier after prange

Every prange in a parallel block now uses "omp for nowait". When code
follows the loop, an explicit "omp barrier" is put after it instead of
relying on the implicit barrier of "omp for". The last statement of a
parallel block, a "parallel for" and a nested prange get no barrier.

Since every loop now has the same pragma, the C code assertions on it
are removed. test_prange_barrier_between_loops still checks the
behavior.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Keep the barrier after the last prange of a block when it has an else clause

The else clause runs after the loop and may read its variables, so the loop
isn't the end of the block.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
